title: Towards Synergistic Teacher-AI Interactions with Generative Artificial Intelligence
extended_summary:
This chapter addresses the growing role of generative AI in education and the concern that it may automate teaching work in ways that reduce teacher agency, cognitive engagement, and professional judgment. Rather than evaluating a single intervention with measured outcomes, the paper proposes a conceptual framework for understanding how teachers and AI interact across different degrees of shared control and mutual adaptation.

The authors introduce five levels of teacher-AI teaming: transactional, situational, operational, praxical, and synergistic. These levels are defined by how information, decisions, actions, and feedback flow between teachers and AI systems, ranging from one-shot request-response use to iterative co-adaptation and potential mutual challenge. The framework is positioned as a way to analyse GenAI-supported teacher-facing tools in educational contexts and to distinguish productivity-oriented automation from deeper cognitive teaming.

To illustrate the framework, the chapter draws on a systematic review of empirical AI-in-education studies from 2010 to 2025, with a secondary focus on GenAI-powered teacher-facing tools. The review suggests that current applications are mostly transactional, situational, or operational, with some praxical examples, but no clear empirical cases of true synergistic teaming. The authors argue that synergy may require stronger teacher AI literacy, better pedagogical design, and more human-centred co-design, while also noting that current GenAI systems may have limited capacity to genuinely push back or negotiate with teachers.

Because this is a conceptual and review-based chapter, it does not report controlled subgroup analyses by teacher experience, subject area, grade band, school context, or deployment format. Its main contribution is a taxonomy and interpretive lens for future empirical work on teacher-AI interactions.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generative AI / large language model-based conversational and multimodal systems used to generate, adapt, evaluate, or provide feedback and instructional content.
identified_tools.use_case: The chapter does not evaluate a single product; it synthesizes empirical examples of teacher-facing GenAI use in education and proposes a five-level teacher-AI teaming framework, including use for feedback generation, lesson planning, tutoring, grading, and situational feedback.

findings.finding_summary: Across the reviewed empirical examples, GenAI was associated with improved efficiency in teacher-facing tasks. The chapter reports that AI-assisted grading decreased grading time by 44% and increased grading accuracy by 6% compared with manual grading, and that co-produced feedback reduced production time while maintaining comparable quality to manual feedback.
findings.measure: Grading time, grading accuracy, feedback production time, and feedback quality in reviewed teacher-facing GenAI studies

findings.finding_summary: The chapter reports that co-produced feedback using GenAI yielded comparable quality to manual feedback and statistically significant learning gains. The text does not provide study-level effect sizes, sample sizes, or confidence intervals for these findings.
findings.measure: Quality of student feedback and learning gains in reviewed studies

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual chapter with a narrative review of prior studies rather than a primary controlled evaluation of a specific tool. The reported evidence is synthesized from other papers and no subgroup or moderation analyses are presented here.
impact_tier_rationale: The chapter describes potentially meaningful practical effects such as reduced grading and feedback time and improved accuracy, but these are secondary summaries without full study details or pooled estimates. The impact direction is generally positive, but the underlying evidence is not directly evaluated in this paper.
